evidence: The original randIntFromRange computed Math.floor(random()*(max-min))+min with no guard, so max<min yields values outside [min,max). 0ddb97c added the guard, but randInt then detected it by e.message.includes('max must be greater than min'), which is what F18 flagged.
guidance_note: When a helper's precondition violation needs to surface as a typed error, validate in the public function that owns the arg positions (randInt) rather than throwing a generic Error and string-matching it on the way back up.

evidence: bodyTypeMismatch('dig', -1, ...) gives a meaningless position, and 0ddb97c threaded argCount through to use argCount-1. Later reviews (#3/F7, #5/F7) say argIndex is documented as 1-based, which would make argCount-1 point at the default arg instead of the dict; the packet does not show that doc, so that part is unverified. The null-guard law has nothing to do with an argument index.
guidance_note: Before choosing an argIndex value, read bodyTypeMismatch's documented index base and check every existing call in the same function against it.

evidence: FailError hard-coded pos {0,0,0}, and evalCommand only re-wrapped TypeMismatchError. 0ddb97c added a pos parameter and an instanceof FailError rethrow with cmd.pos, which is the reviewer's option (b) plus (a).
guidance_note: When adding a new EvalError subclass, mirror every evaluator re-wrap path that existing subclasses go through, so call-site position is attached the same way.

evidence: The original code lowercased any two characters and treated everything but 'pm' as AM, so 'xx' parsed. 0ddb97c throws unless the slice is am/pm. It does this case-insensitively, which is looser than Go's case-specific PM/pm tokens but closes the reported hole.
guidance_note: When porting a strict parser token by token, have each consume step reject input it doesn't recognize, rather than assigning a default.

evidence: The original parseGoLayout loop ended when the layout was exhausted and never compared vp to value.length. 0ddb97c added the 'extra characters' throw, matching Go's extra-text error.
guidance_note: A ported parser should check end-of-input after the scan loop, the same way Go's time.Parse does.

evidence: The datetime index docstring lists 11 functions, and no toDateInZone/mustDateModify/mustToDate exist. The agent edited the PR description to match what was delivered, which is one of the reviewer's two offered remedies.

evidence: The lockfile hunk quoted in #5/F12 shows @noble/hashes@2.2.0 with engines node '>= 20.19.0' against the package's '>=20'. 0ddb97c bumped engines.node to '>=20.19.0'.

evidence: The docstring claimed Node >= 14.17 for globalThis.crypto.randomUUID, which is wrong for Node 14/16 globals. 0ddb97c rewrote it to 'Node >= 20 (per package.json engines)'. The thread's replies describe the README exports fix instead, because the agent posted F8/F9/F10 replies to the wrong threads; the code change itself is correct.

evidence: The README promised Node >= 14.17 against engines '>=20'. 0ddb97c rewrote it to cite '>= 20.19.0 (per engines.node)'. This thread's reply describes the uuidv4.ts docstring fix, so it was another cross-posted reply.

evidence: The 'exports exactly' list lacked FailError, sprigRandom, sprigHash, and sprigDatetime, and 0ddb97c added all four. This thread's reply describes the runtime-floor fix (cross-posted), so the thread record does not match the action even though the commit is right.

evidence: This is a false positive on the flag: 0ddb97c did not touch constraint.ts, so this is pre-review code. The premise holds because the /g TOKEN_RE exec skips non-matching text. The 0894356 fix only checks s.slice(consumed) after the last match, not gaps between matches, which the reviewer's 'after removing matched spans' wording asked for. #5/F1 then caught that gap.
guidance_note: When validating that a tokenizer consumed its whole input, use a sticky (/y) regex or assert m.index equals the previous end on every match, not just after the last one.

evidence: This is a false positive on the flag: constraint.ts was not in 0ddb97c. '~=' was tokenized and mapped to strict equality, while the docstring listed only ~ and ^, and 0894356 removed it. Because the /g regex skips unmatched characters, '~=1.0' now silently parses as '=1.0', the same between-token gap #5/F1 later reports. The agent's parity claim about Masterminds is not verified in the packet.
guidance_note: When removing an operator from a tokenizer, test that input using it is now rejected, not silently re-tokenized.

evidence: This is a false positive on the flag: parse.ts was not in 0ddb97c. \w admits '_', which SemVer 2.0.0 identifiers forbid, and 0894356 replaced it with [0-9A-Za-z-]+(?:\.[0-9A-Za-z-]+)*.
guidance_note: Build a spec-mirroring regex from the spec's grammar character classes, not from \w shorthands.

evidence: This is a false positive on the flag: semver/index.ts was not in 0ddb97c. The owner replied 'We should use the actual type T unless there is a reason not to', and the agent removed returnType entirely, which follows neither reading of that instruction, and justified it with an unrelated null-guard law. The packet does not show what returnType 'T' means in this engine, so the reviewer's claim is unverified.
guidance_note: When the owner gives direction on a thread, either follow it or reply with the specific reason it doesn't hold; dropping the annotation answers neither the reviewer nor the owner.

evidence: This is a false positive on the flag: _format.ts was not in 0ddb97c. String(10).replace(/0+$/,'') gives '1', so ms=10 formats as '.1' instead of '.01'. 0894356 changed it to pad3(z.ms).replace(/0+$/,''), which matches how the 6- and 9-digit variants already pad via fmtFrac.
guidance_note: When a family of tokens shares one shape (.999/.999999/.999999999), implement them through one helper so the narrow case can't diverge from the padded ones.

evidence: 0ddb97c touched _prng.ts but left randString unchanged, so the flag is a false positive. String += in a loop is not O(n^2) in V8 (rope strings), so the agent's 'O(n^2) to O(n)' claim overstates the cost. The array+join change is still harmless, and the owner approved it ('easy and quick fix').

0ddb97c edited _parse.ts only for AM/PM and the trailing-input check; the '.000' cases' 'vp + (val[vp] === "." ? 1 : 0)' code is pre-review, so the flag is a false positive. Making the dot required (0894356) matches Go's stdFracSecond0 handling.
guidance_note: When tightening a parser for one finding (F4/F5 strictness), sweep every token case for the same 'optional where the layout says mandatory' pattern in that pass.

evidence: 0ddb97c's F1 fix introduced 'e.message.includes("max must be greater than min")' in randInt.ts, which is the exact line flagged. 0894356 replaced it with a RandIntRangeError class and an instanceof check; the owner called the original 'terrible'.
guidance_note: Don't detect your own error by its message text; give it a type, or validate where the typed error is built.

narrative: This is a large sprig-expansion PR with ten round-0 findings, all real and all fixed in 0ddb97c. Seven of the eight round-1 findings are on pre-review code the first pass missed, so the round-1 flag is mostly a false positive. Only F18 was caused by the F1 fix, which string-matched its own error message. The F1/F2 argIndex choices also left an unverified 0- vs 1-based question that later PRs re-raise.
guidance_observations: The agent posted the F8, F9, and F10 replies to the wrong threads, so each thread's record describes a different fix than the one it asked for.
Several round-1 replies lost their backticked tokens ('Remove  from TOKEN_RE'), so the reply was sent through a shell that ate the inline code.
On F14 the agent overrode a direct owner instruction without explaining why.

evidence: The docstring still said 'variadic maximum' after the change to Math.trunc(Number(v)). 30909fb updated it to describe truncation toward zero.

evidence: Same as F1, for min.ts; fixed in 30909fb.

guidance_note: When a fix exists to choose one rounding mode, include a test input that distinguishes it from the neighboring modes (a negative fraction for trunc vs floor).

narrative: This is a small trunc fix for max/min. The two docstring findings were accepted and fixed. The description mismatch and the negative-fraction test gap were dismissed with one-word replies, even though the tests as written cannot tell trunc from floor. Round 1 had no findings.
guidance_observations: One-word dismissals ('no', 'ignoring') leave nothing a later reader can check; even a correct rejection needs its reason on the thread.

evidence: Math.min(...args) has an engine argument-count ceiling that the previous reduce did not have. db1a5d5 switched to reduce((m,v)=>Math.min(m,v), Infinity), which keeps NaN propagation and the same empty-args result.

Four of the five round-1 findings re-raise PR #1 issues that 0ddb97c fixed but that 0894356's lineage lacks. evidence: An injected random() outside [0,1) does break randString, randIntFromRange, and shuffle. But the agent clamped to [0, 0.9999999999999999], including NaN, which silently turns a broken PRNG into plausible output. Centralizing at one seam satisfies single-enforcer; the cure should have been to reject the bad value loudly at that seam.
guidance_note: When a caller-injected seam can violate its contract, validate once at the seam and throw; clamping hides the caller's bug.

guidance_note: When a caller-injected seam can violate its contract, validate once at the seam and throw; clamping hides the caller's bug.

narrative: This was the fresh replacement for #3, reviewed at 0894356. Seven of its thirteen findings re-raise PR #1 issues that 0ddb97c had already fixed, because 0894356's lineage lacked that commit. One real finding (F1) is the gap left by the incomplete #1/F11 tokenizer fix. The PRNG findings were cured by silent clamping instead of loud validation, and most threads were resolved without any reply.
guidance_observations: Ten of thirteen threads were resolved with no reply, including the real F1 tokenizer gap, so the record can't show whether that bug was fixed or dropped.
Opening a fresh PR from a lineage that predates the merged fixes cost a whole round of duplicate findings; rebase onto the merged base before requesting review.
